T279.reason: Peer juries supply the specialist judgment behind an award.
Prize competitions promise a reward for a specified goal; awards recognize achievement.
Grants can support work before there is an achievement to recognize.
Status hierarchies help explain why recognition changes whose work gets attention.

T001.reason: Mentorship gives practical judgment a route between people when instructions alone are insufficient.
Introductions give a mentee access to people and opportunities outside their existing network.
Sponsorship for advancement adds advocacy and reputational backing to advice.
Succession planning connects development to the future continuity of a project.
Recurring gatherings create repeated opportunities for mentoring relationships to form.
Office hours offer a bounded way to seek advice without an ongoing mentorship commitment.

S005.reason: Technocracy grounds authority in expertise, which is narrower than the classical aristocratic ideal.
Elections give people a voice in selection without guaranteeing governing ability.
Dynasties make family continuity a route for transferring authority.
Meritocracy also requires a standard of ability, but addresses selection and opportunity more broadly.

T211.reason: Private ownership defines rights over resources exchanged in many markets.
Contracts specify the commitments made in exchange.
Courts provide one institutional route for settling disputes over exchange.
Public provisioning can support shared benefits that are difficult to sell individually.
Free riding helps explain difficulties funding benefits available to noncontributors.
Double auctions are a concrete mechanism for coordinating buyers and sellers.
Capitalism combines market exchange with private investment and control of production.

T339.reason: Trade unions pool workers’ interests and knowledge for collective representation.
Coalitions combine separate groups around a shared public demand.
Petitions make support for a demand visible to decision-makers.
Capture is one possible distortion of organized influence, not a synonym for lobbying.
Representative democracy creates ongoing relationships between constituents and officeholders.
